contexts.text: Why the priests were not to marry widows, (See Virgin.)
They called those in good, widows, etc.

Widows (in the Word) = those who are in a state of good and not so much in truth; and those who are in a state of truth, and not so much in good; and who yet long to be in (truth and good, respectively).
The brother (of the deceased husband) represented a kindred good with which might be conjoined the truth that was represented by the wife who was a widow...
Remain a widow in thy father's house () = an alienation from himself. Explained.

A widow = the truth of the Church without its good. Explained... That is, those who are in truth without good, and still long to be in good, consequently, who love to be led by means of good; a husband = the good which should lead. In the Ancient Church, such persons were understood, in a good sense, by widows, whether they were women or men. For they distinguished the neighbour into classes... and when they spoke of widows, they meant such persons as are in truth without good, and still long to be led by means of good.
That by widows, in a good sense, are signified those persons who are in truth without good, and still long to be led by means of good. Illustrated.

Widows () = those who as adults are in truth, but not yet in good, whose judge is said to be the Lord, because He leads them, and this by means of good into truth, that is, into the truth of intelligence... (For) truth without good, which is the widow, becomes the truth of intelligence by means of a life of good.
To devour widows' houses () = To deprive of truths those who long for them, and to teach falsities.
The widow in Zarephath (to whom Elijah was sent) () represented those outside the Church who long for truth. AC 4844:13. AC 9198:7, Fully explained.
But the widows in the vastated Church, to whom Elijah was not sent () = those persons who are not in truth because not in good; for where there is no good there is no truth.
They who are in such (separated and empty) truth, and also they who are in falsity, are signified by widows in the opposite sense. Illustrated.
As by widows were signified those who are not in truth because not in good, it was reproachful for Churches... to be called widows. Illustrated.

As a widow represented... the truth of the Church without its good... therefore, in the ancient Churches... the priests were forbidden to marry a widow who was not the widow of a priest (; )... The widow of a priest represented the affection of truth from good... and therefore it was also allowed the widows who were the daughters of a priest, who were childless, to eat of... the holy things (). (For this = the appropriation of good after the things not of the Church had been removed... AC 10109:4.)

She removed from upon her the garments of her widowhood () = a simulation of truth from good; for a widow = those in truth without good, yet long to be led by means of good; and the garments with which widows were clothed represented such truth... so that to removethe in = to put off the representation of a widow... and, as she covered herself with her veil, to simulate truth from good.

She put on the garments of her widowhood () = intelligence; for a widow = one in truth without good who longs to be led by means of good; and garments = truths; and these two things taken together = intelligence. Explained. Moreover, a widow, in the genuine sense, = one in truth who longs to be led by means of good into the truth of intelligence. Explained.
(In what sense it is to be understood that good is to be done to widows, etc.)
Under Wife, see this reference.
Truth widowed of good. Explained.
The extinction of their spiritual life is described by widowhood, and bereavement (); widowhood = the privation of truth and thence of good; bereavement = the privation of truth and of good.

Any widow... (ye shall not afflict) () = those who are in good without truth, and yet long for truth... The reason a widow = this, is that a man = truth, and his woman, good; and therefore the woman of a man, who is made a widow = good without truth. But, in a sense still more interior a widow = truth without good, because, in this sense, a husband = good, and his wife, truth... But, as the Celestial Church is not here treated of, but the Spiritual Church, by a widow is signified one in good and not in truth who longs for truth.

There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah () = the state of the acknowledgement, then, of truth Divine in the Church; for widows = those in good without truth... the days of Elijah = the state of the reception of truth Divine... at that time...
Widows (when mentioned with strangers, and orphans) = the conjunction of good with truth.

Your women shall become widows () = that the goods with them will perish... For widows = those in good and not in truths who still long for truths; but here, those who do not long for truth, because it treats of the evil, who afflict widows. (Explained.)

Thou shalt not take the widow's garment in pledge () = not to take away, by any method, the truths which long for good; for... a widow = those in good who long for truths; or, in the abstract, the good which longs for truth; for, if truth is taken away, good and its longing perish.
He ravished their widows () = to pervert the goods which long for truth. AE 601:13.

I am not a widow () = that they will protect themselves; for a widow = one who is without protection, because without a man. The word... widow is used... because there is meant Babylon as a Church. AE 1121, Explained.

(On the) marriage of a youth with a widow... Between a youth and a widow there is not a like initiation to marriage from first beginnings, nor a like progression in marriage (such as there is between a youth and a maiden) because a widow is more at her own disposal than a maiden...
Under Widower, see this reference.
That the state of a widow is more grievous than that of a widower. Explained.
Widows = those who are devoid of truth, yet long for them.
The widows shall be multiplied more than the sand of the sea () = those who are in evil and long for falsities.
I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know bereavement () = to have no lack of followers, dependents, and worshippers. (Compare AE 1121:2.)
The high priest... shall not take a widow... ()... A widow = good without truth, because it has been left by truth, which is the man. Explained.

Elsewhere in the Word, widows = both women and men who are in good and not in truth, and yet long for truth; thus who are without protection against falsity and evil, but who are protected by the Lord. The term is used also in the opposite sense. Illustrated.
